lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございました！　またのご来店、お待ちしております！」
lines.english: “Thank you! We hope to see you again!”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介」
lines.english: “Shusuke.”

lines.japanese: ２１時５０分。最後に残ったお客さまをお見送りすると、マスターが襟元を緩めながらやってきました。
lines.english: It was 9:50 p.m. Once I had seen out our last customer, the boss approached, loosening his collar.

lines.japanese: 「どうだ、怪我の具合は。何度も聞くが、本当にもう大丈夫なのか」
lines.english: “How is the injury? I know I've asked several times, but are you certain you're all right?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はい！　どうもご心配おかけいたしまして！」
lines.english: “Oh, yes! I'm sorry to have worried you!”

lines.japanese: 俺は頭の後ろに手を伸ばし、傷口のガーゼを固定するテープに触れながら笑顔で答えました。
lines.english: Smiling, I reached behind my head and touched the tape holding the gauze over the wound.

lines.japanese: 上から軽く押さえてみても切り傷自体はもう痛みらしい痛みがなく、こぶになっている周辺に鈍い違和感がじんと来る程度です。
lines.english: Even when I pressed it lightly, the cut itself no longer caused any real pain. All I felt was a dull pulse of discomfort around the swelling.

lines.japanese: 聞いたところ、食い逃げ犯は俺が情けなくぶっ倒れてるうちにまんまと逃げおおせたそうで。
lines.english: From what I heard, our dine-and-dasher made a clean escape while I lay there in an undignified heap.

lines.japanese: 俺も日和子さんさえ無事なら、追いかけて一発入れてやろうなんて危険を冒す気はありません。命あっての物種ってやつですが、一応男としては情けなさもあります。
lines.english: As long as Hiyoko was safe, I had no intention of risking my neck by chasing him down to land a punch. Staying alive came first. Still, some masculine part of me found the outcome humiliating.

lines.japanese: 「むしろお役に立てず面目ありませんでした」
lines.english: “If anything, I apologize for being so thoroughly useless.”

lines.japanese: 「たわけが、カジノバーのバウンサーにでもなったつもりか。そんなものは最初からおまえらの仕事じゃないだろう。そんなことより鷲介」
lines.english: “Idiot. Did you think you were a bouncer at some casino bar? That was never your job—or hers—to begin with. More to the point, Shusuke...”

lines.japanese: 彼は従業員を気遣う雇用主の表情で、自分のこめかみをこつこつと叩いてみせました。
lines.english: Wearing the face of an employer concerned for his staff, he tapped his own temple several times.

lines.japanese: 「場所が場所だ。外傷は浅いようだが、短時間とは言え意識を持っていかれたぐらいだ。万一のこともある、きちんと医者に診てもらった方がいいぞ」
lines.english: “The location worries me. The wound may look shallow, but you lost consciousness, however briefly. There could be complications. You ought to have a doctor examine you properly.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい……ですよね……」
lines.english: “Ah, yes... You're right...”

lines.japanese: いいひとだなあマスター。そんな心配するようなことじゃないんだけど、こういうときは俺も真面目に答えておこう。
lines.english: The boss really was a good man. It was hardly worth this much concern, but at a time like this, I ought to give him a serious answer.

lines.japanese: 「そうですね、病院行ってきます。はい今度、ええと、機会があれば」
lines.english: “Yes, I'll see a doctor. Next time—um, when I get the chance.”

lines.japanese: 「ふん。おまえの“機会があれば”は、機会が来た試しがないだろう」
lines.english: “Hmph. Whenever you say ‘when I get the chance,’ the chance never seems to come.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はは……えっと、それじゃあ俺、工藤さんの手伝いに戻りますんで」
lines.english: “Ah, ha ha... Well, I'd better get back to helping Kudo.”

lines.japanese: 俺は一礼して厨房へ向かい、サービス残業の嫌いな先輩アルバイターと共に閉店準備を再開しました。
lines.english: I bowed and headed for the kitchen, where I resumed closing duties beside Kudo, who despised unpaid overtime.

lines.japanese: そして。
lines.english: And then.

lines.japanese: 「お疲れさまっしたあ！」
lines.english: “That's us done! Good night!”

lines.japanese: 現在の時刻、１０時２０分。
lines.english: The time was now 10:20 p.m.

lines.japanese: 閉店から２０分。実際にはラストオーダーが入るちょっと前から動きだしてるので、約一時間で本日のクローズ作業完了ということになります。
lines.english: Twenty minutes after closing. In truth, we had started shortly before the kitchen stopped taking orders, so today's closing work had taken roughly an hour in all.

lines.japanese: 勤務二日目にこの成績は、時間にうるさい工藤先輩にも満足していただけたようでした。
lines.english: For my second day on the job, that result seemed to satisfy even Kudo, a notorious stickler for time.

lines.japanese: まあ、こちらにも急がなければならない事情はありますしね。ええ、今後一層の努力を重ねたい所存にございますよ。
lines.english: Of course, I had reasons of my own to hurry. Indeed, I intended to redouble my efforts henceforth.

lines.japanese: てな話をしつつ、階段のふもとで工藤さんと別れました。彼は個人ロッカーが一階のスタッフルームにあるのです。
lines.english: Talking along those lines, I parted from Kudo at the foot of the stairs. His personal locker was in the first-floor staff room.

lines.japanese: 俺は帰り支度を整えるため、二階のスタッフルームへ向かいました。
lines.english: I headed for the second-floor staff room to get ready to leave.

lines.japanese: 「失礼しまーす」
lines.english: “Coming in.”

lines.japanese: ノックしてドアを開けた先に、ひとの姿はありません。
lines.english: I knocked and opened the door. No one was in sight.

lines.japanese: しかし部屋を仕切るパーテーションの向こうから複数の女性の話し声がします。聞き覚えのある声。紀奈子さんに英里子さんに……お、日和子さんもいるな。
lines.english: Several women's voices came from beyond the partition dividing the room. Voices I knew: Kinako and Eriko... Ah, Hiyoko was there too.

lines.japanese: ふむ。ウェイトレスさんの生着替え（×３）か……。
lines.english: Hmm. Three waitresses changing clothes live and in person…

lines.japanese: フローラルな香りの漂いそうな、魅惑のイマジネーションをかきたてる響き。つい耳をそばだててみたくなるシチュエーションです。しませんけどね。
lines.english: What an enticing phrase, redolent of flowers and rich in fuel for the imagination. The sort of situation that made a man want to prick up his ears. Which I did not do, naturally.

lines.japanese: 「そしたらその先輩が鉄板の上に吐いちゃって、もう、なんで焼肉屋でもんじゃが出るんだっつう話でー」
lines.english: “So then my senior threw up all over the hot plate. I mean, who ordered monjayaki at a barbecue joint, right?”

lines.japanese: だって普通に聞こえてくるんだもん……。
lines.english: It wasn't as though I had to strain to hear her…

lines.japanese: ていうかフローラルには程遠いだろ！　俺は空気中に描いた英里子さんの虚像を手の甲で叩きながら、自分用のロッカーまで歩いていきました。
lines.english: That was about as far from floral as you could get! Swatting the phantom image of Miss Hino out of the air with the back of my hand, I made my way to my locker.

lines.japanese: 「あーあ……もう私、明日からこの制服着ることもないのかー」
lines.english: “Ahhh... Starting tomorrow, I'll never wear this uniform again.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さん、長かったですもんね」
lines.english: “You've been here a long time, Kinako.”

lines.japanese: 「うんー、明日からいないっていう実感いまいち湧かないよねー」
lines.english: “Yeah. It still doesn't feel real that you won't be here tomorrow.”

lines.japanese: お、今度は真面目な話ですか。
lines.english: Oh? A serious conversation this time.

lines.japanese: まー、でもそっすよねえ、寂しっすよねえ。紀奈子さんにはもう明日から会えなくな──
lines.english: Well, yes. It was sad. Starting tomorrow, we would never see Kinako agai—

lines.japanese: 「明日からも普通にごはん食べに来るけどね」
lines.english: “I'll still come by for dinner like always, though.”

lines.japanese: 来るんだ！（いいけど！）
lines.english: You will? (Not that I mind!)

lines.japanese: 「家にいても暇だし」
lines.english: “There's nothing to do at home.”

lines.japanese: 暇なんだ！（勉強しようよ！）
lines.english: You're bored? (Then study!)

lines.japanese: ていうか、よくツッコまないで我慢できるなあのふたり。
lines.english: More to the point, how were those two resisting the urge to call her on any of this?

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さぁん、受験終わったらホントに戻ってきてよー？」
lines.english: “Kinaaako, you really will come back once the entrance exams are over, won't you?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。合格したらね」
lines.english: “Sure. If I pass.”

lines.japanese: 「紀奈子さんは全力さえ発揮できれば大丈夫ですよ。頑張ってください」
lines.english: “If you do your best, Kinako, I'm sure you'll make it. Good luck.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう。ひよちゃんも受かるといいね」
lines.english: “Thanks. I hope you pass too, Hiyo.”
“What?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: な、なんだ？　日和子さんが受かるの受からないのって……彼女、まだ受験生じゃなかったよな。
lines.english: Wh-what was that? What was Hiyoko supposed to pass or fail...? She wasn't taking entrance exams yet.

lines.japanese: じゃあ、またどっかの小説コンテストにでも送ったのか？　いや、でも日和子さんってもう、二作出して担当編集まで付いてるプロ作家なんだから、そんなわけはないか。
lines.english: Had she submitted something to another fiction contest? No, that made no sense either. Hiyoko was already a professional novelist with two books and an editor of her own.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ……そ、そう、ですね、その話はまた今度……」
lines.english: “Ah... Oh. Y-yes, well, we can discuss that another time...”

lines.japanese: 何事かと引きよせられてゆく俺の耳、しかしもつれて曖昧になってゆく日和子さんの声。
lines.english: My ears strained toward her, drawn by the mystery, while Hiyoko's voice tangled itself into uncertainty.

lines.japanese: 「そ、それじゃ私、お先に失礼します」
lines.english: “W-well, I'm heading out. Good night.”

lines.japanese: あれ、ついに逃げちゃったよ。
lines.english: Oh. She had fled altogether.

lines.japanese: いや、待て。それはつまり、更衣室を出る＝こっちに来るってことじゃないか。
lines.english: No, wait. Leaving the changing area meant coming this way.
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: 「ごごっ、ごめんなさい！　お、おつ、お疲れさまです！」
lines.english: “I-I-I'm sorry! G-good night!”

lines.japanese: べつに盗み聞きとかしてたわけじゃなし、何も後ろめたいことなんかないのについ動揺してしまう俺は、もはや日和子さんと目が合えば竦みあがってしまう体質なのかもしれません。
lines.english: I hadn't been eavesdropping, and I had nothing to feel guilty about. Yet I flustered all the same. Perhaps merely meeting Hiyoko's eyes had become enough to make my entire body seize up.

lines.japanese: 「……ど、どうもです」
lines.english: “...G-good night.”

lines.japanese: 私服姿の日和子さんは、出会い頭の俺の狼狽っぷりが伝染したのか、心持ちあとじさりしつつ視点を脇へ泳がせました。
lines.english: Hiyoko, now in her street clothes, seemed to catch my discomposure the instant we met. She edged half a step backward, her gaze darting away.

lines.japanese: あれ、なんか珍しい反応だな。いつもは目を逸らすにしても、もっとこう「ふ……」って食後の大型獣みたいに悠然とそっぽ向くひとなのに。
lines.english: That was unusual. Even when she looked away from me, she normally did it with a languid ‘hmph,’ like some great beast reclining after a meal.

lines.japanese: 「ど、どうですか」
lines.english: “H-how is it?”

lines.japanese: 彼女が斜め下の何もない床を見ながら言いました。
lines.english: She spoke while staring at an empty patch of floor below and to one side.

lines.japanese: 「え、なにがですか？」
lines.english: “How is what?”

lines.japanese: 聞きかえすと日和子さんは、自分の後頭部に手を添えてみせながら、ちらりと俺を見上げました。
lines.english: At my question, Hiyoko placed a hand against the back of her own head and flicked one glance up at me.
“Your injury...”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、怪我ね！　はい、もう全然！」
lines.english: “Oh! Right, the injury! It's completely fine now!”

lines.japanese: 俺も患部に触れて答えるものだから、なんだかふたりして「どうもどうも」のポーズ。
lines.english: I touched the injured spot as I answered. With one hand behind each of our heads, we looked like two people apologizing past each other.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さんの方こそ大丈夫でした？　駄目ですよ、女の子はああいう手合いを追っかけちゃ」
lines.english: “More to the point, were you all right? You can't go chasing men like that, Hiyoko. You're a girl.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、店長にも同じことを言われました。本当にすみませんでした、私のせいで」
lines.english: “Yes. The Manager said the same thing. I am truly sorry. You were hurt because of me.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　あ、いや、そういうことじゃなくて！　日和子さんと俺の怪我は関係ないです、ええ！」
lines.english: “What? Oh, no, that isn't what I meant! You had nothing to do with my injury. Nothing at all!”

lines.japanese: 「でも、私をかばって」
lines.english: “But you shielded me.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……でも、それはだって、そもそも俺が逃げなきゃ、日和子さんのとこに椅子が飛んでくこともなかったわけで──」
lines.english: “Yes, but only because if I hadn't dodged in the first place, the chair would never have gone flying toward you—”

lines.japanese: 「あの、座ってください」
lines.english: “Please sit down.”

lines.japanese: 有無を言わせぬ芯の通った声が、俺の言葉を途中で遮りました。彼女は四本指で俺にソファーを勧めながら、事務机に向かって移動します。
lines.english: A firm voice that permitted no argument cut me off. She indicated the sofa with four straight fingers and moved toward the office desk.
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「少々お時間いただけませんか。傷の経過を見せてもらいたいんです」
lines.english: “May I have a little of your time? I'd like to see how the wound is doing.”

lines.japanese: そして机の前で屈みこみ、机の最下段の引き出しから救急箱を引っぱりだしました。
lines.english: She crouched before the desk and pulled a first-aid kit from the bottom drawer.

lines.japanese: 「お帰りの前にガーゼを交換させてください」
lines.english: “Let me replace the gauze before you go home.”

lines.japanese: 思わず俺の手は、耳の後ろの応急処置が施されている箇所にふたたび移動していました。
lines.english: My hand returned involuntarily to the place behind my ear where the first aid had been applied.

lines.japanese: 「え、うそ、じゃあ……ひょっとして、これやってくれたのって……」
lines.english: “Wait, seriously? Then... Don't tell me you're the one who did this...”

lines.japanese: 「私ですけど、なにか」
lines.english: “I am. Is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: 衝撃のあまり言葉が出てきませんでした。
lines.english: The revelation struck me speechless.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、まずこれ剥がしますね」
lines.english: “I'll remove this first, then.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、お手数かけます……」
lines.english: “Y-yes. Sorry to trouble you...”

lines.japanese: ……ごくり。
lines.english: ...Gulp.

lines.japanese: なんだろう、この緊張感。あの玉泉日和子さんがいつになく親和的な申し出をもって、しかしいつもと変わらぬ無表情で俺の真後ろに立っています。
lines.english: Why was I so nervous? Hiyoko Tamaizumi herself had made an uncharacteristically friendly offer, yet now stood directly behind me with precisely her usual lack of expression.

lines.japanese: ぺり、ぺり、ぺりぺりぺり……。
lines.english: Peel... peel... peel-peel-peel...

lines.japanese: 息詰まる沈黙の中、日和子さんの手によって俺の頭髪から粘着テープが剥がされていきます。慎重な速度でちりちり毛根を引っぱってゆく痛みが、ああ、まるでこの状況を暗示しているかのよう。
lines.english: In breathless silence, Hiyoko peeled the tape from my hair. At that painstaking pace, it tugged every strand with a prickling pain at the root. Ah, how perfectly the pain seemed to foreshadow the course of this encounter.

lines.japanese: うーん、こういうのは一気にベッと行ってくれちゃった方がマシだと思うんだけどいたっ！　痛っ、痛っ！　ちょっ、痛たたた……！
lines.english: Hmm. I really thought it would hurt less if she tore it off all at—ow! Ow, ow! Wait, owowow...!

lines.japanese: 「痛くないですか」
lines.english: “Does it hurt?”
“Not at all!”

lines.japanese: ああっ、俺いま考えるより先に答えてたけど、うそうそ痛いです痛いです！　ていうか、俺の立場でこういうこと言うのもなんだけど、このひともしかして剥がすのヘタじゃね！？
lines.english: Ah! I had answered before I could think, but that was a lie—it hurt, it hurt! And I knew I was in no position to complain, but was she possibly terrible at removing tape!?

lines.japanese: みりみりみりみり……どべりっ！
lines.english: Riiip-rip-rip-rip... RRRIP!
“Yeeow!”

lines.japanese: がくっ。
lines.english: I sagged.

lines.japanese: 「うん、もう塞がってるみたいですね」
lines.english: “Yeah, looks like it’s already closed up.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうですか……」
lines.english: “I-is that so...?”

lines.japanese: 麻酔なしレーザーメスのような痛みの照射が終わって、ちょっとばかり温度の上がった声が降ってきました。ああ良かった。いろんな意味で。
lines.english: The beam of pain from her anesthetic-free laser scalpel ceased, and a voice several degrees warmer descended upon me. Oh, thank goodness. In several senses.

lines.japanese: すると今度は耳元でプシュッと音がして、患部周辺の頭皮に細かな水気が降りかかってきました。たぶん消毒液のスプレーでしょう。
lines.english: Then came a spritz beside my ear, and a fine mist settled over the scalp around the wound. Disinfectant spray, presumably.

lines.japanese: 「沁みませんか」
lines.english: “Does it sting?”

lines.japanese: 「沁みませんよ」
lines.english: “Not at all.”

lines.japanese: 垂れてるけど。
lines.english: It was dripping, though.

lines.japanese: ティッシュか何かで大部分は塞きとめているものの、その隙間を縫ってしずくがつつーっと。
lines.english: She had blocked most of it with a tissue or something, but one drop found a gap and slid down.

lines.japanese: うーん、ひょっとして日和子さんって頭脳労働に秀でている分、手先の方は不調法なのかな。あーあー、垂れてる垂れてる。
lines.english: Hmm. Perhaps the same gifts that made Hiyoko so brilliant at intellectual work had left her hopelessly clumsy with her hands. There it went. Still going.

lines.japanese: ぬ、く、垂れた水滴が微妙に気になるな……ていうか、こそばゆい……そういや髪の根元って感じやすいっていうか、むしろ性感帯だってひともいるぐらいだしな。
lines.english: Nngh. That trickling drop was becoming strangely hard to ignore… In fact, it tickled… Come to think of it, the roots of the hair were sensitive. Some people even considered the scalp an erogenous zone…

lines.japanese: あ、ああッ！　こ、今度はうなじをつたって……う、うひい背中へ！
lines.english: Ah—ahh! N-now it was running down the nape of my neck… E-eek, onto my back!

lines.japanese: ふぬう！　くくく、くしゅぐったい！　ひいッ！　ら、らめえ、声出しゃう～！
lines.english: Nnngh! T-t-tickles! Eek! N-nooo, I'm gonna cry out!

lines.japanese: <10>\　鷲介、とんじゃうううう！
lines.english: Shusuke's gonna fly awaaaaay!

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん。くねくねしない」
lines.english: “Chitose. Stop squirming.”

lines.japanese: 「しゅ、しゅいましぇん」
lines.english: “Sh-shorry.”

lines.japanese: 「次。軟膏塗ります」
lines.english: “Next. I'm applying the ointment.”

lines.japanese: ぬるっ。
lines.english: Slick.
“Ahhn!”

lines.japanese: 「い、痛かったですか！？」
lines.english: “D-did that hurt!?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……いえ、そういうわけでは」
lines.english: “Ah… No, that isn't it.”

lines.japanese: 「え、じゃあいまの悲鳴はなんですか」
lines.english: “Then what was that cry just now?”

lines.japanese: 「訂正。実はちょっぴり痛かったんです」
lines.english: “Correction. It did hurt a tiny bit.”

lines.japanese: 「そうですか、やっぱり……すみません、優しく塗ります」
lines.english: “I thought so… I'm sorry. I'll rub it in gently.”

lines.japanese: <8>\「優しく塗ります！？」
lines.english: “Rub it in gently!?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なにか問題が」
lines.english: “I-is there a problem?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、ないです！　なんにもないです、なんでもないです！」
lines.english: “Ah, no! No problem! Nothing at all, never mind!”

lines.japanese: ただの狩男病です。
lines.english: Just a case of Karuo syndrome.

lines.japanese: 「そうですか？　それじゃあ、続けますね……」
lines.english: “Are you sure? Then I'll continue…”

lines.japanese: ぬるんっ。
lines.english: Sliiick.
“Nooo!”

lines.japanese: 俺は学習しない男だった。
lines.english: I was a man incapable of learning.

lines.japanese: 本日の教訓。馬鹿に塗る薬はない。
lines.english: Today's lesson: there is no ointment for stupidity.

lines.japanese: 「千歳さん？　終わりです、お待たせしました」
lines.english: “Chitose? I'm finished. Sorry to keep you waiting.”

lines.japanese: 「え……あ、ああ、そっすか」
lines.english: “Huh…? Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 美貌の才媛の献身的な指先によって体の敏感な部分に粘液を塗りたくられていた俺は（←狩男的表現）、現実の声に呼ばれて桃源郷から帰還しました。
lines.english: The devoted fingertips of a brilliant beauty had been smearing viscous fluid all over a sensitive part of my body (← Karuo's phrasing), and the voice of reality called me back from paradise.

lines.japanese: 「おおーっ」
lines.english: “Ooh!”

lines.japanese: 頭の後ろに手を伸ばして、新しくなったテーピングに触れてみました。触ったところで見えやしないし、なんだかよくは分からないんだけど、初めての制服に袖を通したときのような小さい感動が湧きあがります。
lines.english: I reached behind my head and touched the fresh tape. Touching it did not let me see it, of course, and told me very little, yet a small thrill rose inside me—the kind one feels upon slipping into a brand-new uniform for the first time.

lines.japanese: ていうか、まあ、あの日和子さんが俺のためにしてくれたっていう事実がね。嬉しいじゃないですか。わざわざ手ぇ汚して頑張ってくれたんですよ彼女、ねえ、不器用だてらに──いや、不器用とか言うなよ。
lines.english: More than anything, it was the fact that Hiyoko had done this for me. How could that fail to make me happy? She had gone to all this trouble and dirtied her hands, clumsy though she was—no. Don't call her clumsy.

lines.japanese: ようし、俺もうこのテープとガーゼ、一生剥がさないぞう。なんて、アイドルに握手してもらった少年ばりに不衛生な思いがこの胸をよぎったとか、よぎらなかったとか。
lines.english: Excellent. I would never remove this tape or gauze for the rest of my life. A thought as unsanitary as a boy refusing to wash the hand his idol had shaken may or may not have crossed my mind.

lines.japanese: 「ありがとうございます！　千歳鷲介、感激です！　こんばんは！」
lines.english: “Thank you! Shusuke Chitose is deeply moved! Good evening!”

lines.japanese: 「べ、べつに、大したことじゃ……」
lines.english: “I-it was nothing worth making such a fuss...”

lines.japanese: うわあ、日和子さんが謙遜してるう。
lines.english: Wow. Hiyoko was being modest.

lines.japanese: ははは、可愛いとこあるじゃないですか、不器用だてらに──いや、不器用カンケーないだろ。
lines.english: Ha ha ha. She had her cute side after all, clumsy though she was—no, her clumsiness had nothing to do with it.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんなことより……あの、今日もお帰りの際、持ちだしていただいて結構ですから」
lines.english: “M-more to the point... You may take it home again when you leave tonight, if you wish.”

lines.japanese: 彼女はあからさまに話を逸らしたいようで、例の分厚いファイルが眠るキャビネットの最下段を四本指で指ししめしました。
lines.english: Plainly desperate to change the subject, she indicated with four straight fingers the bottom drawer of the cabinet where that infamous thick binder slept.

lines.japanese: ははは、この美貌の才媛め。その話さえすれば、またすぐ俺がおとなしくなるとでも思っていやがるな！
lines.english: Ha ha ha, you beautiful intellectual. You think mentioning that will instantly make me meek and obedient again!

lines.japanese: <-6>\「き、機会があれば」
lines.english: “W-when I get the chance.”

lines.japanese: まあ、おとなしくなるんですけど。
lines.english: Which, admittedly, it did.

lines.japanese: しかし、そうやって俺が目を落としてもじもじしていると──
lines.english: But as I lowered my eyes and fidgeted—

lines.japanese: 「くすっ」
lines.english: “Hee hee.”

lines.japanese: ──不意に耳慣れない、優しげで楽しげな息遣いが聴こえてきました。
lines.english: —an unfamiliar breath reached my ears, soft and full of amusement.

lines.japanese: 「またそれですか？　もう、千歳さんの機会っていうのは、いつになったら訪れるんだか」
lines.english: “That again? Honestly, Chitose, when is this ‘chance’ of yours ever going to come?”

lines.japanese: おもてを上げると、日和子さんがマスターと同じようなことを、マスターの数万倍ぐらい愛嬌のある笑顔でおっしゃっていました。
lines.english: I raised my face. Hiyoko had said almost exactly what the boss had said, but with a smile tens of thousands of times more charming.

lines.japanese: そんなこと言われたら、機会もたちまち降臨しようってもんですよ。
lines.english: When she put it that way, the opportunity could hardly help materializing that very instant.

lines.japanese: 「そそ、そうですねえ……まあ、あしたは定休日だし……？」
lines.english: “W-well, yes... And tomorrow is the restaurant's regular day off, after all...?”

lines.japanese: 俺はさっき日和子さんが指したキャビネットへ、吸いよせられるように歩いていきました。
lines.english: As though pulled by an invisible force, I walked toward the cabinet she had indicated.

lines.japanese: 「うん、マニュアルねえ。ちょっと持って帰って、家でも読みすすめておこうかな」
lines.english: “Yeah, the manual... Maybe I’ll take it home and keep reading there.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: すると日和子さんはそれを不本意ながらの言動だと捉えたようで、凛とした眉を八の字にして上品に微苦笑されました。
lines.english: Hiyoko seemed to take this as a show of reluctance. Her proud eyebrows folded into a worried arch, and she offered me a refined, rueful smile.

lines.japanese: 「いいですよ、無理しなくて。あの、私、考えたんですけど──」
lines.english: “You needn't force yourself. I have been thinking, and—”

lines.japanese: 「あーん？　おめ、まーだマニュアル全部読めとか言ってんのー？」
lines.english: “Huh? You still telling him he's gotta read that whole manual?”

lines.japanese: 更衣室のドアが開き──室温を下げるような声と共に現れたのは、帰宅準備の済んだ英里子さんでした。
lines.english: The changing-room door opened, and Eriko emerged ready to leave, accompanied by a voice that seemed to lower the room's temperature.

lines.japanese: 「千歳だってもう、マニュアルのおおよそには目ぇ通しおわってるでしょ。まだ足りないとこあれば、あとは現場出てから少しずつ読んできゃいいんじゃん？　ねえ？」
lines.english: “Chitose has already looked over most of the manual, hasn't he? If there are still things he doesn't know, he can read up on them little by little once he starts working the floor. Right?”

lines.japanese: 彼女はそう言って、分厚いファイルを両手に抱えている俺へ、あの強さと優しさを兼ねそなえた眼差しを向けられました。
lines.english: She said this while giving me—standing there with the thick binder in both arms—her familiar look of strength tempered by kindness.

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか。このひとはこのひとなりに、俺をかばってくれているわけか。
lines.english: Oh, I see. In her own fashion, she was standing up for me.

lines.japanese: だけど、どのみちその件に関しての言葉を持たない俺は「あー」と唸りながら、ちらりと玉泉トレーナーを窺いました。
lines.english: But I had nothing to contribute either way. I merely groaned, ‘Uh...’ and stole a glance at Coach Tamaizumi.

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは考えこむように、あるいは表情を隠すように、ゆるく握った手を口元へ運びました。
lines.english: As though deep in thought—or perhaps concealing her expression—Hiyoko brought one loosely curled hand to her lips.

lines.japanese: 「だって、あした──は定休か、あさってから紀奈子さんいないんだよ？」
lines.english: “Besides, tomorrow—oh, right, we're closed. Starting the day after tomorrow, Kinako won't be here.”

lines.japanese: そのあいだにも英里子さんは、可愛い年下の男の子のため容赦なく続けます。
lines.english: Still championing her adorable younger colleague, Eriko pressed on without mercy.

lines.japanese: 「研修も結構だけど、いいかげんフロアに千歳回してもらわないと、ヘルプの意味ねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Training's all very nice, but if you don't put Chitose on the floor soon, having him here as extra help is pointless.”

lines.japanese: 「いいよ。じゃあ、もし千歳が勉強不足で問題起こしたら、うちらが責任取るよ。ねえ、紀奈子さーん？」
lines.english: “Fine. If Chitose causes trouble because he hasn't studied enough, we'll take responsibility. Right, Kinaaaako?”

lines.japanese: 「え、えええ、えぇーとぉー……」
lines.english: “Wh-what? Um, well, I...”

lines.japanese: 更衣室を出たところでおろおろしていた紀奈子さんは、いつものように仲介の言葉が見つからず縮こまっていました。
lines.english: Kinako had just emerged from the changing area. Caught between them, she shrank into herself, unable as ever to find the words that might make peace.

lines.japanese: 俺は溜息を吹きあげて前髪を揺らしました。しばしの間。
lines.english: I blew a sigh upward, stirring my bangs. For a little while, no one spoke.

lines.japanese: ややあってから、日和子さんが口元の手を下ろし……英里子さんに向かって答えました。
lines.english: At length, Hiyoko lowered the hand from her mouth... and answered Eriko.

lines.japanese: 「──正論ですよね」
lines.english: “—You're right.”

lines.japanese: あれ、意外にあっさりした反応……。
lines.english: Oh. That surrender came with surprising ease...

lines.japanese: 「だろ？　ほら千歳、もう読まないでいいってさ」
lines.english: “See? There you go, Chitose. She says you don't have to read any more.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いえ、俺の担当は玉泉トレーナーですから」
lines.english: “Oh, no. Coach Tamaizumi is in charge of my training.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。いいんだろ、たまひよー」
lines.english: “That's what I mean. We're good, right, Tama-chick?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。千歳さんには次回から、フロアの仕事に就いていただきます」
lines.english: “Yes. Beginning with your next shift, Chitose, you will be assigned to the dining room.”

lines.japanese: 「いままでご苦労さまでした」
lines.english: “Thank you for all the work you've put in.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは俺の前に立ってファイルを奪い、唇の両端が妙に皺深い笑顔をこしらえました。
lines.english: Hiyoko stepped in front of me, took away the binder, and fashioned a smile with strangely deep creases at either corner of her mouth.

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょっ……い、いんすかそれで？」
lines.english: “W-wait... a-are you sure you’re okay with that?”

lines.japanese: 俺は慌てて彼女の手からファイルを取りかえしました。
lines.english: In my alarm, I snatched the binder back from her hands.

lines.japanese: 「はい。英里子さんのおっしゃることはもっともですし──」
lines.english: “Yes. Eriko's argument is entirely reasonable, and—”

lines.japanese: 「──いえ、違うんです。なんだか後出しっぽくなっちゃったけど、本当は私、英里子さんに言われる前からそのことを考えてたんです」
lines.english: “—No, that isn't what I mean. I know it sounds as though I'm only claiming this after the fact, but I really had been thinking the same thing before Eriko said it.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、でもそれは……」
lines.english: “Yes, but...”

lines.japanese: それはたしかに、そうなのかもしれないけど、でもそんな簡単に折れちゃったら──
lines.english: That might well be true. But if she gave way so easily—

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、なんだか日和子さんの考えが間違ってたみたいじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Then it makes it sound as if your whole idea was wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「ってゆーなら、間違ってたんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Maybe that's because it was wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「いやいやいや！」
lines.english: “No, no, no!”

lines.japanese: そんなことはない。間違ってるわけじゃない。決して間違いではないんだ。ただ、定められた時間の中では他に優先すべき事項があるってだけで──
lines.english: That wasn't true. She hadn't been wrong. Absolutely not. It was simply that, within the limited time available, other matters demanded priority—

lines.japanese: つまり？　うん？　なんだ、簡単な話じゃないか。
lines.english: In other words? Hmm? Why, this was perfectly simple.

lines.japanese: 定められた時間の中で優先されなかった事項は、定められた時間の外へ持ちだせばいい。
lines.english: Anything denied priority within the allotted time could simply be carried beyond it.

lines.japanese: それが俺のタマイズム。
lines.english: That was my Tamaism.

lines.japanese: 「分かりました。はい。千歳鷲介、次回からフロア担当として務めさせていただきます」
lines.english: “Understood. Very well. Beginning with my next shift, I, Shusuke Chitose, shall serve upon the dining-room floor.”

lines.japanese: 俺は英里子さんに敬礼なんてしてみせて、それから別の腕に替えて、日和子さんにも敬礼を送りました。
lines.english: I saluted Eriko. Then I switched arms and offered Hiyoko a salute as well.

lines.japanese: 「ということになりましたので、それまでにマニュアルは全部読んでおきます」
lines.english: “That being settled, I will finish reading the entire manual before then.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「はああ？」
lines.english: “Huuuuh?”

lines.japanese: 「なにしろ機会が生じましたんで」
lines.english: “After all, the chance has presented itself.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんや英里子さんがまた何か言いださないうちに、俺はさっさと分厚いファイルを自分のロッカーまで運んで、バッグの中へ押しこんでしまいました。
lines.english: Before Hiyoko or Eriko could raise another objection, I hurried the thick binder over to my locker and forced it into my bag.

lines.japanese: よい、しょっと。
lines.english: Hup.

lines.japanese: 「機会が生じましたんで！」
lines.english: “The chance has presented itself!”

lines.japanese: さらに繰りかえしキラリと光る白い歯を日和子さんに向けたつもりが、彼女は微妙な表情でどこか斜め下に視線を落としていました。
lines.english: I repeated myself and flashed what I intended as a gleam of white teeth at Hiyoko. Wearing an uncertain expression, she lowered her gaze off to one side.

lines.japanese: ちぇ。
lines.english: Tch.

lines.japanese: 「さぁー、べんきょーべんきょー」
lines.english: “All riiight—time to study, time to study.”

lines.japanese: 勤勉な男を大声でアピールしながら、俺はひどく重たくなったバッグを担いで更衣室へ下がりました。
lines.english: Loudly advertising my diligence, I shouldered my considerably heavier bag and retreated into the changing area.
“Phew...”

lines.japanese: 首をコキコキ鳴らしつつ、片手でシャツのボタンを上から外し、残る手でベルトを引っこぬいたとき。
lines.english: I cracked my neck, unbuttoning my shirt from the top with one hand while pulling off my belt with the other. Then—
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: そのときになって俺はふと忘れものに気付きました。
lines.english: Only then did I remember something I had forgotten.

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうだ日和子さんっ！」
lines.english: “Th-that's right! Hiyoko!”

lines.japanese: 昨日に引きつづき、帰り際のお約束。
lines.english: Our customary end-of-day ritual, following yesterday's precedent.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん！　きょ、今日こそいっしょに帰っ──」
lines.english: “Hiyoko! T-today, surely we can walk home togeth—”

lines.japanese: 俺は足をもつれさせながら飛びだしましたが、そこに残っていたのは年上のおねえさんふたりだけでした。
lines.english: I burst out with my feet tangling beneath me, but only the two older women remained.

lines.japanese: 「ひよちゃん？　もう行っちゃったよ？」
lines.english: “Hiyo? She already left.”

lines.japanese: 「……まじすか」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっかあ。ふられちゃったねえ、二日連続」
lines.english: “Oh, right. She turned you down two days in a row. Poor thing.”

lines.japanese: 「……ふう、やれやれ。逃げ足の速い仔猫ちゃんだ」
lines.english: “...Good grief. What a fleet-footed little kitten.”

lines.japanese: 「いいからおまえ、ズボン上げろよ」
lines.english: “Whatever. Pull your pants up.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃっ！　なんかスースーすると思ったら！」
lines.english: “Eek! I thought there was an awful draft!”

lines.japanese: 俺は足元で輪を作っていた制服のスラックスを慌てて拾いあげました。
lines.english: I hurriedly pulled up the uniform trousers pooled in a ring around my ankles.

lines.japanese: 「でも、千歳君ほら。きょうはべつに断られたわけじゃないから、がっかりすることはないさ」
lines.english: “But look, Chitose. She didn't actually turn you down today, so there's no reason to be discouraged.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか。それもそっすね。さすが紀奈子さん、頭いいなあ」
lines.english: “Oh, that's true. You're right. Brilliant as ever, Kinako.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもどうせ見込みないんだから、結果は早い方がいいんじゃないの」
lines.english: “Yeah, but since he doesn't stand a chance anyway, isn't it kinder to get the answer sooner?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、ちょっとアナタ！　そこの付け睫毛のひと！　なんすかもう、縁起でもないこと言わないでくださいよ！」
lines.english: “W-wait just a moment, you! The woman with the false eyelashes! What's that supposed to mean? Don't say things like that!”

lines.japanese: 「いいからおまえ、ズボン上げろって」
lines.english: “Whatever. Pull your pants up.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃあっ！　やっぱりスースーすると思ったら！」
lines.english: “Eek! I knew there was an awful draft!”

lines.japanese: 俺は肩をすぼめてふたたび足元の輪を拾いあげました。ああ、しまった、ベルトは更衣室に置きっぱなしだったんだ。
lines.english: Hunching my shoulders, I once again hauled the ring of cloth up from my feet. Ah, damn it. I had left my belt in the changing area.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ、まったく。みんなでパンツ見せたり見せられたり、とんでもない破廉恥レストランですねここは」
lines.english: “Honestly. Everybody showing their underwear to everybody else—what an appallingly indecent restaurant this is.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　おまえの他に、誰が誰に見せたんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Who's shown anybody their underwear besides you?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえまあ、その……なんていうか、言葉のあやなんですけどね」
lines.english: “Oh, well, that was... you know. Merely a figure of speech.”

lines.japanese: 「おいおい、こちとら嫁入り前だぞ。言葉のあやで露出狂にされたら、たまったもんじゃねっつーの」
lines.english: “Hey, some of us are unmarried women with reputations to protect. I'm not letting a figure of speech turn me into an exhibitionist.”

lines.japanese: 「まったくですね。好き好んで他人に下着を見せるような品位のない人間にはなりたくないものです」
lines.english: “Quite right. One hopes never to become the sort of shameless person who displays their underwear to strangers for pleasure.”

lines.japanese: 「いやだからおまえ、ズボン上げろっての」
lines.english: “No, I'm telling you to pull your pants up.”

lines.japanese: どっかーん！（爆発オチ）
lines.english: Kaboom! And scene.

lines.japanese: ふぅーっ……。
lines.english: Phewww...

lines.japanese: さてさて、今日も一日ご苦労さん、と。
lines.english: Well. That was another day done.

lines.japanese: あしたはアレキサンダーの定休日。夕方に米田さんとのアポがあるから、それ以外の時間を使ってマニュアルをだーっと一気に読破──
lines.english: Tomorrow Alexander would be closed. I had an appointment with Yoneda in the evening, but I could use the rest of the day to tear through that manual in one tremendous burst—

lines.japanese: ──ま、まあ、さすがに一日じゃ無理かな。
lines.english: —w-well, perhaps a single day was asking too much.

lines.japanese: 思いつきで大変な約束をしてしまった、数分前の自分に後悔しないこともないですが……いや、大丈夫！　鷲介くんはやれば出来る子！
lines.english: I couldn't entirely deny regretting the enormous promise I had made on a whim several minutes ago... No, it would be fine! Shusuke could do anything once he applied himself!

lines.japanese: いささか頼りなげにくすぶる意欲のほむらを胸に、俺はゆっくり目を閉じて深呼吸しました。
lines.english: With the none-too-reliable flame of motivation smoldering in my breast, I slowly closed my eyes and drew a deep breath.

lines.japanese: おやすみなさい。
lines.english: Good night.
